name: Maaseiah
overview: Maaseiah was a male biblical figure known for being sent by King Josiah to oversee the repair of the house of the Lord. While his tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded, his role in this significant religious restoration effort highlights his trusted position during Josiah's reign.
namesAndTitles: The name Maaseiah means 'YHWH is a refuge,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that underscores God’s protection. This proper name, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 34:8, reveals a connection to divine refuge, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Maaseiah beyond what is listed in his role sent by Josiah. No additional familial connections are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Maaseiah’s significance lies in his involvement in the restoration of the temple under King Josiah, a pivotal moment in the biblical narrative emphasizing the renewal of true worship and covenant faithfulness. His role demonstrates the cooperation of God’s people in preserving the sanctity of the Lord’s house, which was central to Israel’s spiritual revival.
